description: Proper nouns (people, places, organisations, units, weapons) and unambiguous loanword nouns that the non-dialogue surfaces still render in Japanese. Mined by tools/mine_ui_facing_terms.py against the promoted tip and translated by hand. This is the proper-noun slice of the 489 'safe' candidates; the other 445 are deliberately NOT taken (see _why_only_proper_nouns).
_marker_note: marker is not declared here on purpose: the installed Hangul run marker is read from tools/hangul_marker.py (out/patch/hangul_char_map.json). A frozen value here goes stale on retarget and writes a real character instead.
_why_only_proper_nouns: The 489 'safe' candidates are shared prose vocabulary, so localizing one puts Korean inside an otherwise-Japanese sentence. For grammar words that is strictly worse than leaving it alone, and for verb stems it is broken: 背負 + って -> 짊어って. Those stay Japanese.

A NAME does not have that problem. 다카르 reads as Dakar wherever it lands, it takes no inflection, and it is the same category the shipped unit_names_ko / weapon_names_ko catalogs already cover. The residual mixed-particle text around it (다카르に) is pre-existing, not caused by this row.

Pronouns are excluded even though they are the highest-volume candidates (オレ x163, オマエ x81, ボク x67, 貴様 x65, キサマ x51, アタシ x42, アナタ x37, アンタ x14). They are grammar-bearing and compose: オレ inside オレたち gives 나たち. The katakana-glue test does not catch that because たち is hiragana, so it is scored 'particle' rather than 'broken_word'.
Slang / common nouns excluded for the same reason: アホ ウソ ヒマ ムチャ ブザマ ゴメン タダ マズイ イジメ オタク オッサン オモチャ オサラバ ホント カンタン マネ ハ－ト クセ カギ エサ アゴ パパ カトンボ.

Shouts and onomatopoeia excluded: フィンガァァァ－－ッ ガトォォ－－ッ ギャンギャン. They are elongation runs, and Korean must never carry the '－' (it is scored broken_word and cannot be told from a truncated katakana word).
Uncertain referents dropped rather than guessed: フォン (von / phone), イ－ズ, キリング.

REMOVED after measuring the rendered text: バオア and スオ－ノ. Both are only ever one component of a middle-dot compound name (ア・バオア・ク－ = A Baoa Qu, テラ・スオ－ノ), so localizing the component alone renders ア・바오아・ク－ — a name half in each script. The other components (ア, ク－, テラ) are unsafe fragments, so there is no whole-word fix; leaving them Japanese is correct. scan_fragment_composition_hazard treats U+30FB as a separator on purpose (ハマ－ン・カ－ン really is two words), which is right for personal names and wrong here; scan_mixed_script_artifacts now reports this as severity 'split_compound'.
_selection_rules: every row was reported 'safe' (not 'glued') by tools/mine_ui_facing_terms.py on the promoted tip, so it is not a mid-word fragment of a longer Japanese word
no row duplicates a jp key already shipped in another data/*_ko.json

every ko was proved encodable against the INSTALLED tbl + marker before this file was written — this is the missing-Hangul-glyph failure class that produced the name75 encode_fail rows, and it cannot be caught by eye
verify with tools/scan_fragment_composition_hazard.py and tools/scan_mixed_script_artifacts.py after applying
_verified: 44 proposed / 44 passed the pre-write checks / 2 removed afterwards on rendered-text evidence (バオア, スオ－ノ) = 42 shipped
